clue.text: Mark of rank taken by King Harry

parts.note: a badge is an emblem worn to show rank
R, for Rex, is the usual abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An officer's insignia is snatched by a monarch called Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the king's name, but it is a verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to pester them persistently, the same as hounding them.

clue.text: Something hurting at end of facial hair

indicators.note: only the closing stretch of the word for facial hair is kept, the front being dropped

parts.note: a moustache is hair grown on the upper lip

explanation.surface: A painful spot at the tip of someone's beard or moustache.
explanation.walkthrough: The last four letters of MOUSTACHE are kept; 'at end of' says to drop MOUST from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain or dull soreness is something that hurts.

clue.text: Pounds on the door?

parts.note: suggests someone banging at a door, but means pounds sterling taken at the entrance

explanation.surface: Someone hammering at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' reads as a verb of knocking; it is money, collected at the gate of a sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission receipts taken from spectators at a match or show are money paid at the entrance.

clue.text: Some more pastrami makes a meal

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bit more cured beef is enough for lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for a meal or feast; the clue's 'makes' is a link, so the sense is a meal.

clue.text: Book a woman into bed? On the contrary

indicators.note: says one piece goes inside another
reverses the stated direction, so the bed takes in the woman rather than the woman going into bed

parts.note: a dame is a woman, especially an older one

explanation.surface: A risqué suggestion to take a woman to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' reverses the clue's own instruction: the container and contents swap roles. The book is George Eliot's 1859 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's first full-length novel, a well-known Victorian book.

clue.text: Wills and Harry? Troublesome pair, as Anne heard

indicators.note: something troublesome is disordered, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Princess Anne overhears that her nephews Prince William and Prince Harry are a difficult pair.
explanation.walkthrough: Wills is Prince William; royals are said to need an heir plus a reserve in case.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince William is the successor and Harry the reserve, the classic royal pairing of firstborn and backup son.

clue.text: Criminal deserving the firing squad?

parts.note: a firing squad usually executes, but here firing means setting fire to things

explanation.surface: A villain who ought to be shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The firing squad is not an execution: a squad that does firing would be fire-raisers.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who deliberately sets property alight is a criminal whose offence is fire-raising.

clue.text: Having lesson in parts, messenger lacking English

indicators.note: says the letter for English is missing from the messenger word

parts.note: a bearer carries a message or letter

explanation.surface: A courier with school lessons in segments, without his English class.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'lesson' as 'less on': having less on is being more undressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing fewer clothes means being more naked, a comparative of nude or exposed.

clue.text: Force randy Greek to swerve

indicators.note: swerving changes course, so the letters veer into a new order

explanation.surface: Compel a lustful Greek to change direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The unseen agent thought to drive the universe's accelerating expansion, treated as a cosmic force.

clue.text: Circling Shed 26, old man taps cheek

indicators.note: says the taps go round everything else

parts.note: taps are marked C and H, for cold and hot
a hut is a shed
Z is the 26th letter of the alphabet
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: An old man going round a shed taps someone on the cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is not a clue number here but the alphabet position of Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazen nerve or impudence, from Yiddish, is what cheek means.

clue.text: Arrest criminal John-Paul!

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: A cry to apprehend a crook named John-Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: The philosopher is Jean-Paul; 'John-Paul' is an English rendering of his name, whatever the blogger says.
explanation.definitionFit: The French existentialist philosopher's forenames were Jean-Paul, the French form of John-Paul.

clue.text: Native American at the Alamo, say, quietly getting overinvolved?

parts.note: the Alamo in Texas was a Spanish mission
the Cree are a Native American people
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A Native American at the Texas fort who quietly gets too involved.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the gradual expansion of an operation beyond its first aims, a slide into deeper commitment.

clue.text: Animosity about responsibilities is concerning rogues

indicators.note: says the animosity word goes round the other

parts.note: pique is resentment
cares are worries or duties

explanation.surface: Resentment over one's duties is about scoundrels.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes fiction recounting the adventures of a roguish hero.

clue.text: Indicate private is about to be canned?

indicators.note: with canned, says the turned letters end up inside the tin symbol

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin, so canned means put in tin

indicators.note: says the private's letters are turned round

parts.note: a GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: Signal that the soldier is going to be fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canned' looks like slang for sacked; it means enclosed in Sn, tin's chemical symbol. 'about' turns GI to IG.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a signal or gesture is to indicate.

clue.text: Told to go into a communal meeting? One didn't

indicators.note: says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for shared work, such as a sewing bee
sent means despatched

explanation.surface: Instructed to attend a community gathering, someone stayed away.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest: one who did not go into the meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stays away from where they are expected is a non-attender.

clue.text: Horror film making a fortune about initiation into sex

indicators.note: says the rearranged letters go round the single letter
making of the letters means forming something new from them
the start of a word, its first letter

explanation.surface: A scary movie earns millions by introducing sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges A FORTUNE into NOFERATU; 'about' puts it round S, the first letter of 'sex'.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1922 German silent vampire picture is a classic of the scary-movie genre.

clue.text: Main road more important, it's said, for one leaving the country

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI

indicators.note: says the word is only to be spoken, its sound kept, its spelling dropped

parts.note: greater means of more importance

explanation.surface: A main road matters more, people say, to someone emigrating.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 stands in for I.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant or bird that travels abroad seasonally is one who leaves home.

clue.text: One spotted boy by turning one way

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: says the little word by is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone noticed a lad as he turned a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' reads as seen, but means covered in spots.
explanation.definitionFit: The red beetle with black dots is the archetypal spotty insect.

clue.text: Plant elder, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a culinary herb with grey-green leaves
a wise old person, an elder being one example

explanation.surface: A shrub such as the elder.
explanation.walkthrough: The elder looks like the shrub, which keeps it beside 'Plant', but it is a senior person.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb and the wise person share a name.

clue.text: Hidden in dead part of Australia

parts.note: the late so-and-so is someone dead
NT is the Northern Territory

explanation.surface: Concealed in the outback's empty interior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden in' tempts a search for letters concealed in the next words; 'Hidden' is the definition, 'in' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant and not yet showing is concealed.

clue.text: Little fellow in conflict with car — this will provide comprehensive support

indicators.note: says the little fellow sits inside the conflict word

parts.note: war is conflict
an elf is a small sprite
an estate is a British car with a large rear load space

explanation.surface: A small man rowing over a car, while something supports everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: The government system of benefits and services supports citizens from cradle to grave.

clue.text: Love affair with office work? Not I

indicators.note: says the letter I is dropped

parts.note: filing is routine clerical work

explanation.surface: A romance with office duties, but not for me.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief romantic or sexual relationship is a short affair.

clue.text: Cry, then one needed to lighten up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a light bulb is needed to brighten a room

explanation.surface: Weep, then someone must cheer up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighten up' looks like cheer up; 'up' turns the word for a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep noisily, a colloquial word for crying.

clue.text: Member of large family in the way gets a funny look

indicators.note: says the family member goes inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
a quin is one of quintuplets

explanation.surface: A child from a big family stands in the road and gets a strange glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideways or narrowed glance is an odd look.

clue.text: In a fit, people easily influenced

indicators.note: says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: able means fit or capable
men means people

explanation.surface: People who are swayed easily in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' reads as a seizure; it means able.
explanation.definitionFit: Compliant and open to persuasion.

clue.text: Endlessly continue holding tool in dish

indicators.note: says the shortened word goes round the tool
says the last letter is removed

parts.note: to keep on is to continue
an edger trims lawn edges

explanation.surface: Keep going while holding a utensil in the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Indian rice dish with smoked fish and eggs is a breakfast meal.

clue.text: So doctor held these up for approval

indicators.note: says the doctor is gripped inside the word for so

parts.note: thus means so
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical degree

explanation.surface: A doctor raises them to show she approves.
explanation.walkthrough: Holding them up shows approval, so the definition runs on through 'up for approval'.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised digits signal agreement, the gesture for approval.
